A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCIF benchmark. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained appendices A–E with v3's added Appendix F.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 23 models, modality ablations, and question-answering breakdowns in Tables 2, 9–10 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and analyses, reports revised numerical results, and adds model-output failure examples in Table 11.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and fixed/mixed instruction framework are retained, with no new model, algorithm, or inference component. Expanded annotation documentation does not establish a changed method; the individual evaluation-prompt revision is assessed under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ACL 2023 material: 21 core talks, 100 talks for summarization, and 220 QA pairs across four languages and 13 tasks. The added descriptions of topics beyond NLP and recording diversity do not establish additional evaluated data or scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 23 models, including Gemini 2.5 Flash. The comparator memberships in the modality ablation and four-model QA breakdown also remain unchanged. Table 11 illustrates failures of already evaluated models.

E3.justification: Table 7 changes the first German MCIFmix summarization prompt from at most 200 words to approximately 200 words; Table 4's fixed prompt remains unchanged. Metrics, sample counts, model configurations, and generation limits are otherwise retained. The PDFs do not establish reruns or explain the larger numerical revisions.

E4.justification: New Appendix F and Table 11 provide six groups of concrete failure examples, including slide copying, partial transcription/translation, hallucination, wrong-language output, irrelevant QA responses, and refusals. v2 discussed these failure patterns without displaying these outputs. Existing modality ablations and QA breakdowns remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars for the benchmark results. Averaging across languages remains unchanged and is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 9–10 extensively replace summarization scores and MiniCPM-o-2's long-form results. In Table 2, its MCIFmix WER changes from 98.2 to 179.2, COMET from 39.1 to 25.9, and QA BERTScore from 22.9 to -38.4. The MCIFfix summarization leader changes from Llama 3.1 at 18.1 to Aya Expanse at 25.1. These are substantial reported-result revisions, with their computational cause unspecified.

T1.justification: Neither version develops a theoretical contribution through formal assumptions, theorems, derivations, or proofs. The retained task descriptions and standard metric explanations introduce no changed mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows the prompt-robustness claim from instruction variation generally to controlled reformulation preserving semantic equivalence. The abstract changes the novelty wording from multilingual to crosslingual and explicitly mentions topics beyond NLP. The central benchmark contribution and broad model limitations remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly limits the evaluation to simple, single-turn instructions and discusses multimodal fusion, sequence compression, and extended context modeling as future directions. Section 5.1 additionally explains that GraniteSpeech may return a transcript instead of answering a question. Most existing interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly details domain-specialist review of transcripts and checks for guideline compliance, terminology, and consistency. The professional staffing totals, compensation, annotation tools, model settings, hardware, and access information were already documented. The additions clarify quality control without establishing that the dataset was rebuilt.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gaido et al. (2024) and references on prompting, alignment, contrastive instruction tuning, data selection, and chain-of-thought reasoning, mainly supporting the expanded future-work discussion. The related-work survey and positioning against existing multimodal benchmarks remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence is retained, with localized prose edits and an expanded conclusion. Appendix B replaces two numbered subsections with separate transcription, QA, translation, and consistency discussions. Publication headers and author contact text also change, without extensive paper-wide rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-page failure-example Table 11, revises Figure 2's axes and legend, and replaces dashes with LONG labels for textual tasks in Table 1. Appendix material is repositioned relative to its tables. Most existing table structures and visual designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Expanded expert-review documentation, concrete failure examples, and narrower claims improve transparency. However, substantial unexplained result revisions introduce a table–figure conflict: MiniCPM-o-2's long-form MCIFmix WER changes from 98.2 to 179.2 in Table 2, while Figure 2 still plots approximately 98. These reporting benefits and numerical consistency problems prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
